UI/UX Designer
01

Research

I learn the problem before I draw anything. Competitive analysis shows what already exists; quantitative and qualitative research shows what people actually need.

What I do
  • Competitive analysis
  • Quantitative & qualitative research
  • User personas
  • Customer journey mapping
  • Affinity mapping
  • Card sorting
What you get
PersonasJourney mapsPrioritised feature list
In practice · HayWay

Personas and journey maps showed payment confusion, fare splitting and scheduling as the main rider frustrations. Feature prioritisation turned them into the MVP scope.

02

Structure

Before visuals, I decide how the product is organised and how people move through it. Wireframes let me test the idea while it is still cheap to change.

What I do
  • Information architecture
  • User flows
  • Low-fidelity wireframes
  • User testing
  • Iteration on feedback
What you get
SitemapUser flowsWireframes
In practice · Skatey

Market and competitor analysis became clear category navigation, so beginners and pros both reach the right skates in a few taps.

03

Systems

High-fidelity prototypes bring the design to life, and a design system keeps it consistent as the product grows and more people build on it.

What I do
  • High-fidelity prototypes
  • Design systems
  • Reusable components
  • Hand-off to developers
What you get
Interactive prototypeComponent libraryDesign system
In practice · ISAA · Bizzy

At ISAA I refine design-system foundations and add components for product teams. At Bizzy, one component system serves both the website and the admin panel.

All work
Mobile app

HayWay

Taxi apps in Armenia made payments confusing and splitting a fare awkward. I ran personas, journey mapping and feature prioritisation to set the MVP, then designed flows, wireframes and prototypes.

OutcomeBooking with transparent pricing and shared fares
Built onReusable component library
Full case on Behance
01Challenge

Riders in Armenia deal with confusing payments, awkward fare splitting and no easy way to plan a trip ahead.

02Approach

Personas, customer journey mapping and feature prioritisation defined the MVP. Then user flows, wireframes and prototypes.

03Result

A booking flow with transparent pricing and shared fares, plus “Booking rides for future” to schedule trips ahead. Built on a reusable component library.

Key screens
  1. 01Onboarding
  2. 02Map with pick-up and destination
  3. 03Ride booking

01Challenge

Buying skates online is hard for beginners and slow for pros: many models, sizes and categories.

02Approach

Market and competitor analysis turned into personas and journey maps, then clear navigation: Products, Accessories, Sales, Support.

03Result

A bold storefront with a seasonal “New arrivals” hero, filter chips on mobile, visible discounts and a direct “Buy now”, on a flexible design system.

Redesign

Meduza News

Instant updates, breaking news. A redesign concept that brings Meduza’s news, blitz news and podcasts together in a calm dark interface on the phone and on the web.

TypeConcept redesign
PlatformMobile app · Website
Full case on Behance
01Goal

Bring news, podcasts, audiobooks, stories and books into one place that is quick to scan.

02Structure

Top navigation for each content type, a home built from “News today” and “Blitz news”, and a mobile tab bar: Home, Favorite, Saved, Settings.

03Interface

A calm dark UI with one amber accent, bookmarkable news cards with publish time, and a podcast library with episode counts and a quick “Listen”.
